criterion: Any one successful changed behavioral observation for a Git revision whose static AST import source closure is unchanged is a counterexample.

estimated_performance.method: sum observed all-oracle subprocess times for assessable revisions minus selected-target oracle times and measured index computation; checkout and clone overhead excluded
estimated_performance.limitation: Not a complete performance test under preregistration: 56 comparisons unassessable and only one oracle per repo, so savings estimate is descriptive.

mathematical_counterexample: Two revisions with the same tracked import-closure Git blob identity can have distinct observable behavior; therefore import-closure identity alone is insufficient to guarantee observational equivalence.
limitations: Deliberately constructed adversarial modifications, not real defects discovered in the third-party projects.
Historical commits tested against newest pinned baseline and may include intentional API evolution; 56 were unassessable with Python 3.13 and the frozen oracle.
Standalone static-AST import-only predictor is the tested object; this does not rule out a stronger analysis that includes implicit package initialization or other runtime dependencies.
Previous h11 evidence index can accept explicitly expanded source closures. These results do not imply that all conceivable evidence indices are unsound.
Time savings estimate excludes clone and checkout costs and is not a benchmark of long-running independent contract suites.
The report was produced in GitHub CI; full result JSON SHA-256 is available in logs but not archived as an artifact.
Upstream repos and h11 master were not modified; adversarial Git commits existed only inside ephemeral CI runner.
